transcript:
Speaker A: chote shahar se sapne lekar badi city aai thi. mehnat karke naukri to mil gai par office ke pehle hi din ehsaas hua ki yahan degree se zyada aapki english mayne rakhti hai. meeting room mein sab baithe the. boss ne kaha please introduce yourself! main khadi hui. sabki najrein mujhpar thin. maine shuru kiya my.. my.. name, i am coming from aur phir main atak gai. ghabrahat mein galat bol diya. sab dheere se hansne lage. maine turant baithte hue bahana banaya. sorry, meri tabiyat theek nahin hai. gale mein problem hai. us din ke baad se main office mein sabse katne lagi. koi baat karne aata to main kaam ka bahana bana deti. email likhne mein ghanton lag jate. dar lagta ki kahin galti na ho jaye. school mein kabhi english bolna sikhaya hi nahin gaya tha to ab kaise seekhti. ek din washroom mein maine do ladkiyon ko baatein karte suna. [I came to the big city with dreams from a small town. I got a job through hard work, but on my first day, I realized English matters more than a degree here. Everyone was in the meeting room. The boss said, 'Please introduce yourself!' I stood up. All eyes were on me. I started, 'My... my... name, I am coming from...' and then I froze. I said something wrong out of nervousness. Everyone started laughing quietly. I immediately sat down and made an excuse: 'Sorry, I'm not well. I have a throat problem.' After that day, I started avoiding everyone at the office. If someone came to talk, I'd make an excuse about work. Writing emails took hours. I was afraid of making mistakes. English speaking was never taught in school, so how would I learn now? One day in the washroom, I overheard two girls talking.]
Speaker B: yaar pata nahin isko job kaise mili. ek sentence english ka dhang se bol nahi pati. pata nahi kahan kahan se aa jaate han. gaon ki gawar kahin ki. [Friend, I don't know how she got this job. She can't even speak one sentence of English properly. Don't know where they come from. What a village rustic.]
Speaker A: wah baat mere kanon mein teer ki tarah lagi. gaon ki gawar kya meri sari mehnat, meri degree ki koi keemat nahin thi sirf isliye kyunki meri english kamjor thi. us din maine decide kiya ki ab bahane nahin banaungi. office ke baad ek spoken english class join ki. mahine ke 4000 rupaye aur batch mein 30 log. teacher aage grammar ke rule likhti rahi. main peeche baithi notes banati rahi. bolne ka mauka kabhi mila hi nahin. phir ek moti grammar ki book khridi. tenses, articles sab rat liye. par jab office mein bolne ki bari aati, sab bhool jati. likhi hui english aur boli jaane wali english donon alag duniya thi. ek raat thaki hari phone chala rahi thi. tabhi youtube par ek english seekho app ka video dekha. mujhe laga ye mere jaise logon ke liye hi bana hai. app download kiya. yahan koi boring lecture nahin. expert bilkul basic se hindi mein samjhate hain wahi english jo office mein logon se baat karne mein roj chahiye aur sabse best cheej thi ai coach disha. usse main apne kamre mein akele bina kisi dar ke bol ke practice karti thi. wo mujhe sahi sentence batati, mere doubts clear karti. wahi cheese jo class mein nahin mili. bolne ka mauka bina sharm ke yahan roj milta tha. roj ke 15 se 20 minute video dekhe aur practice ki aur mera confidence dheere dheere wapas aane laga. phir ek day wahi colleague mere paas aai ek project discuss karne. is baar main chup nahin rahi. maine confidence se kaha 'I have reviewed the project details, I think you've put the wrong number here please check it again.' wah hairan rah gai. uske chehre ki havaiyan ud gai thi aur tab laga maine sirf english nahin seekhi thi. maine apni ijjat wapas kama lee thi. aaj mujhe kisi bahane ki zaroorat nahi. english na aana meri galti nahin thi par use na seekhna meri haar hoti. agar tum bhi sirf english ki wajah se peeche rah rahe ho to english seekho, download karo aur apni pehchan khud banao. install now par click karo aur abhi english seekho app download karo. [Those words hit me like an arrow. 'Village rustic'—was my hard work and degree worthless just because my English was weak? That day, I decided no more excuses. I joined a spoken English class after office. 4000 rupees a month and 30 people in a batch. The teacher kept writing grammar rules on the board while I sat at the back taking notes. I never got a chance to speak. Then I bought a thick grammar book. I memorized tenses and articles. But when it was time to speak at the office, I forgot everything. Written English and spoken English were two different worlds. One night, tired, I was scrolling through my phone. Then I saw a video for the English Seekho app on YouTube. I felt it was made for people like me. I downloaded the app. No boring lectures here. Experts explain from the basics in Hindi, teaching the exact English needed for daily office conversations. And the best part was the AI coach, Disha. I practiced speaking with her alone in my room without any fear. She corrected my sentences and cleared my doubts. The one thing I didn't get in class—a chance to speak without shame—I got here every day. I watched videos and practiced for 15-20 minutes daily, and my confidence slowly returned. Then one day, that same colleague came to discuss a project. This time I didn't stay quiet. I confidently said, 'I have reviewed the project details, I think you've put the wrong number here please check it again.' She was stunned. The color drained from her face, and that's when I realized I hadn't just learned English; I had earned my respect back. Today, I don't need excuses. Not knowing English wasn't my fault, but not learning it would have been my defeat. If you are also lagging behind just because of English, download English Seekho and build your own identity. Click 'Install Now' and download the English Seekho app today.]
